Distinguishes the collective defeat of all four descendants from Jonathan's individual victory.
Requires tracking the officer across quoted dialogue to identify whose predicted death occurs.
Clearly distinguishes the prophet who rides from the sons who saddle his donkey.
Tests the meaningful difference in participants between two consecutive covenants.

Separates Uzziah's explicitly stated reason for leaving from the priests' preceding action.
Presents the king's conjecture as the Arameans' actual expectation without preserving that attribution.
Clearly distinguishes the men's chosen course from an alternative they explicitly reject.
“Who kills first” loosely asks for narration order across separate battles.

Separates Elisha's response to the officer's doubt from his earlier prediction about prices.
